name: @argszero/dsh-phantom-tool-call-guard
description: An empty-identity tool call can be advertised but never answered: tool/call is admitted with callId "", the harness's own assembler only synthesises a fallback id for a missing one (nullish, so an empty string defeats it), and the paired tool/result is then refused at the write boundary with 'requires toolCallId matching its tool source' - before a single byte lands. The log keeps a dangling tool/call, and every later turn re-fails at the same seq, so the session is dead from that point. This plugin sits on the llm/stream waterfall's RETURNED chunk stream - the one seam that reaches both what the loop assembles and what it records - and supplies the missing identity before the call is ever advertised, so the call becomes answerable: it is dispatched, fails honestly as an unknown tool, and the session survives. mode observe counts the same decisions and changes nothing; mode suppress drops the block instead, which is the max-tokens-truncation posture; mode off installs no listener. Zero runtime dependencies, fail-open, no sandbox changes.
